name: What is the difference between stucco patching and stucco re-dashing?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between stucco patching and stucco re-dashing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Stucco patching focuses on repairing specific damaged areas, such as cracks, holes, or localized crumbling, by applying new material to blend with the existing finish. The goal is to seamlessly integrate the repair without altering the overall stucco surface. Stucco re-dashing, on the other hand, involves applying a new finish coat over an entire existing stucco surface, often to refresh its appearance, change its texture, or provide an additional layer of protection. While patching is localized, re-dashing covers a larger, continuous area for a uniform new look.
acceptedAnswer.description: Stucco patching repairs specific damaged spots to blend with the existing finish. Stucco re-dashing applies a new finish coat over an entire surface to refresh appearance or change texture.
